mechanism_narrative: A rise in GDP indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or GDP growth is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate below 1% triggers an increase in borrowing and spending, stimulating economic growth and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 1% (t-test p > 0.05), or the federal funds rate is not negatively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or payroll employment growth is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during expansionary periods (t-test p > 0.05), or industrial production growth is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate below 5% and an increase in housing starts indicate a strong labor market and increased economic activity, leading to higher demand for goods and services, which in turn drives up stock prices, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the unemployment rate is below 5% and housing starts are above 800 (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction between the unemployment rate and housing starts is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, stimulating economic growth and resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is below 1% and the money supply is above 400 (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction between the federal funds rate and the money supply is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment is above 130 and the unemployment rate is below 6% (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction between payroll employment and the unemployment rate is not positively correlated with stock prices.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production and an increase in the consumer price index indicate decreased economic activity and increased inflation, leading to lower demand for goods and services, which in turn drives down stock prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when industrial production is below 90 and the consumer price index is above 250 (t-test p > 0.05), or the interaction between industrial production and the consumer price index is not negatively correlated with stock prices.
